title: Ramayana Trailer Takes China by Storm as Viewers Call It Superior to Hollywood
excerpt: Nitesh Tiwari's epic crossed a million views in China within hours, with Chinese audiences praising its scale and lamenting that local filmmakers can't match it.
body:
• The Ramayana trailer crossed a million views on Chinese social media within hours, generating thousands of overwhelmingly positive comments.
  • Chinese viewers praised the film's grand scale, calling it superior to both Hollywood blockbusters and homegrown Chinese productions.
  • Many Chinese audiences lamented that their own filmmakers have failed to give Chinese mythology the same cinematic treatment.
  • The film is set for a historic global release across 50,000 international screens, distributed by Sony Pictures outside India.

A Million Views and Counting

https://youtube.com/watch?v=HLAyM6vsQcA

Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana, already one of the most anticipated Indian films in history, has found an unexpected wellspring of enthusiasm in China. The trailer crossed a million views on Chinese social media platforms within just a few hours of its release, accompanied by thousands of comments — the vast majority glowing with praise.

Chinese viewers were stunned by the film's production scale, with many commenting that the visuals surpass what both Hollywood and China's own film industry have been delivering. One viewer wrote that the visuals were "stunning" and "a world apart from those cheap fantasy dramas with green screen," while another added, "You can always trust Indian mythological movies."

"Those visuals are stunning. Truly a world apart from those cheap fantasy dramas with green screen."

— Chinese social media user

Chinese Filmmakers Face Uncomfortable Comparison

The most striking thread running through Chinese reactions was self-reflection. Many viewers bemoaned that local filmmakers are unable to give Chinese mythology — which boasts equally rich source material in epics like Journey to the West and Fengshen Yanyi — the same treatment that Ramayana delivers.

The comparison cuts deep in a market where big-budget fantasy and mythological productions have struggled to balance spectacle with storytelling. While China's film industry has produced effects-heavy blockbusters, critics have often noted an over-reliance on CGI without the narrative weight to match. Ramayana, by contrast, has drawn praise for marrying breathtaking spectacle with emotional depth.

The positive reception also reflects Ramayana's pre-existing cultural footprint in China. The epic is familiar to Chinese audiences through the Jataka tales, with the heroics of Lord Rama and Hanuman woven into Chinese folk traditions. Several adaptations have previously been dubbed and released in China under titles such as Sacred Lord.

India's Most Expensive Film Eyes Global Dominance

Billed as the most expensive Indian film ever made, with a reported budget of ₹1,500 crore, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Yash as Ravana, and Sai Pallavi as Sita, alongside Sunny Deol as Hanuman and Ravi Dubey as Lakshman. The score by Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman has further fueled expectations.

The film is being positioned as a global cinematic event. Sony Pictures is distributing it internationally across an unprecedented 50,000 screens. An English-language trailer, featuring AI-powered lip-sync technology developed by DNEG's proprietary Brahma AI system, dropped earlier this month to widespread acclaim. The technology allows actors to appear to speak fluent English with natural lip movements, eliminating the jarring disconnect of traditional dubbing.

"The heart of it is human. All the emotions are human. What the technology is doing is making it look seamless."

— Namit Malhotra, Producer

What It Means for Indian Cinema Globally

Ramayana: Part 1, produced by Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios in association with Yash's Monster Mind Creations, will hit theatres worldwide on November 6, coinciding with Diwali. Part 2 is slated for Diwali 2027.

For the Indian diaspora, the film represents a landmark moment — the first time an Indian mythological epic has been positioned with the same global marketing muscle as a Marvel or DC release. For audiences in China and elsewhere, it signals that India's film industry is now capable of competing at the highest levels of visual spectacle while drawing from its own civilizational stories.

The Chinese reception, in particular, suggests that Ramayana's commercial potential extends far beyond traditional diaspora markets — a development that could reshape how Indian cinema approaches international distribution for years to come.
nri_angle: Ramayana's global release across 50,000 screens marks the first time an Indian mythological epic has been positioned for worldwide audiences, a moment of cultural pride for the diaspora.
